title: Topic 1: Watching Movies
content:
1. Do you often watch movies in your free time?
2. What is your favorite movie or genre, and why do you like it?
3. What meaningful lessons have you learned from watching movies?

questions.answer: Yes, I am a big fan of watching movies in my spare time, usually twice a week.
questions.example: I often watch films on my laptop at home on Friday nights or go to the cinema with my friends at the weekend.
questions.q: Do you often watch movies in your free time?
questions.reason: It is advantageous to my mental health because it helps me relax my mind, recharge my batteries, and reduce stress after a busy week.

questions.answer: My favorite movie genre is comedy, though I also enjoy documentaries.
questions.example: Last Saturday, I watched a funny family comedy with my best friend while eating popcorn, and we laughed the whole time.
questions.q: What is your favorite movie or genre, and why do you like it?
questions.reason: Comedies are relaxing and interesting because they make me laugh out loud and elevate my mood, while documentaries are educational and help me broaden my horizons.

questions.answer: Movies have taught me many meaningful lessons about family love, friendship, and never giving up.
questions.example: For example, after watching a movie about a hardworking student, I learned how to stay patient and keep trying toward my study goals.
questions.q: What meaningful lessons have you learned from watching movies?
questions.reason: Good films give me a deeper understanding of people, culture, and real-life values, and motivate me when I face difficulties.

content:

questions.answer: It took place about three months ago in the main hall of my university.
questions.example: The contest started at 8:00 AM on a Sunday morning, and around fifty students from different classes took part in it.
questions.q: When and where did that competition take place?
questions.reason: Joining an event on campus was very convenient, and having my friends there cheered me up and made me feel more confident.

questions.answer: Yes, academic and sports competitions are very popular at my school and in my city.

Situation: You have an important upcoming exam at school and want to choose the best place to study and revise. There are three options:
- At the school library (thư viện của trường)
- At a quiet coffee shop (quán cà phê yên tĩnh)
- At home (ôn thi tại nhà)

Which option do you think is the best choice and why?
title: Part 2 - Situation 1: Choosing a Place to Prepare for an Exam
content:
Situation: You have an important upcoming exam at school and want to choose the best place to study and revise. There are three options:
- At the school library (thư viện của trường)
- At a quiet coffee shop (quán cà phê yên tĩnh)
- At home (ôn thi tại nhà)

Which option do you think is the best choice and why?

chosen.khen1Text: because the school library has air-conditioned rooms, free Wi-Fi, and quiet study areas that give me the best conditions to revise for the exam.

khen2ARE.answer: Studying at the school library gives me the opportunity to increase knowledge and focus better on my exam materials.
khen2ARE.example: For example, I can review printed textbooks and past exam papers for two hours after class without looking at my phone too much.
khen2ARE.reason: Printed books in quiet libraries protect our eyes from blue-light strain, allow our brain to exercise, and let me find reference materials easily when I have questions.

chosen.khen3Text: an inspiring learning environment where seeing other students study hard motivates me and helps me feel fully confident before the exam.

rejected.reason: buying drinks at a coffee shop every day costs too much money for a student, and customers talking or background music can still break my focus.
revising at home makes it easy to get distracted by family noise, household chores, or the habit of lying down and surfing social media instead of studying.

gives me the opportunity to increase knowledge
printed books in quiet libraries protect our eyes from blue-light strain
an inspiring learning environment ... feel fully confident

title: Part 3 - Topic 1: Benefits of Charity Work and Volunteering
content:
Topic: Benefits of doing charity work and volunteering
Suggestions:
- Helping disadvantaged people in the community
- Developing empathy, teamwork, and social skills
- Bringing a sense of purpose and personal fulfillment
- [Your own ideas]

Follow-up questions:
1. Why should young people and students take part in charity activities?
2. What kinds of charity work are most common in Vietnam?
3. How can organizations make sure charitable donations are used transparently?

hint.coreTopic: benefits of doing charity work and volunteering

followUps.answer: I think young people and students should take part in charity activities because it is a gateway to self-discovery and learning essential life skills.
followUps.example: For example, university students joining a summer volunteer trip to rural areas learn how to work in teams and solve daily problems independently.
followUps.q: Why should young people and students take part in charity activities?
followUps.reason: Volunteering helps students broaden their mind beyond textbooks, meet like-minded people, and appreciate what they already have.

followUps.answer: There are some common kinds of charity work in Vietnam, such as donating blood, giving free meals to hospital patients, and raising money for flood victims.
followUps.example: For instance, many volunteer groups cook hundreds of free lunch boxes outside big hospitals in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi every week.
followUps.q: What kinds of charity work are most common in Vietnam?
followUps.reason: These activities directly solve urgent problems and support people facing illness or natural disasters.

followUps.answer: I think organizations must share clear public reports, while the government should introduce stricter rules and heavy fines for dishonest groups.
followUps.example: For example, a charity group can post bank receipts and photos of delivered supplies online every month so every donor can check them.
followUps.q: How can organizations make sure charitable donations are used transparently?
followUps.reason: Clear records and strong rules help prevent cheating, protect charity money, and keep public trust in charity work.

mindmapPoints.cue: Helping disadvantaged people in the community
mindmapPoints.expand: because sharing food, clothes, or free lessons makes a great contribution to improving their living standard.
mindmapPoints.impact: Therefore, it is good for building a kind and supportive society.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Doing charity work allows people to help disadvantaged people in the community.

mindmapPoints.cue: Developing empathy, teamwork, and social skills
mindmapPoints.expand: For example, working in a volunteer group to clean a park or teach poor children teaches you how to adjust and adapt to the social environment.
mindmapPoints.impact: Clearly, it is beneficial to your personal growth and social network.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Volunteering helps young people develop empathy, teamwork, and social skills.

mindmapPoints.cue: Bringing a sense of purpose and personal fulfillment
mindmapPoints.expand: This is because helping others makes you feel peaceful, elevates your mood, and gives you a deeper understanding of real life.
mindmapPoints.impact: So, it has positive effects on your mental health and life perspective.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Charity work helps volunteers gain a sense of purpose and personal happiness.

Tiêu đề đề bài: Part 2 - Situation 2: Choosing a University Based on Key Criteria
Nội dung chi tiết:
Situation: A high school graduate is deciding which university to apply to and is weighing three main factors:
- The university's ranking (xếp hạng của trường đại học)
- Distance from home (khoảng cách từ nhà đến trường)
- Tuition fee (mức học phí)

Which factor do you think is the most important and why?
title: Part 2 - Situation 2: Choosing a University Based on Key Criteria
content:
Situation: A high school graduate is deciding which university to apply to and is weighing three main factors:
- The university's ranking (xếp hạng của trường đại học)
- Distance from home (khoảng cách từ nhà đến trường)
- Tuition fee (mức học phí)

Which factor do you think is the most important and why?

chosen.khen1Text: because choosing a university close to home saves daily travel time, and living with parents makes living costs easy for the family to afford.

khen2ARE.answer: Choosing a university at a convenient distance from home is advantageous to a high school graduate's mental health and overall well-being.
khen2ARE.example: For example, a student who takes only twenty minutes by bus to campus can save energy for evening study and still have dinner with their parents.
khen2ARE.reason: Because they do not spend hours on congested roads or feel lonely living far away, they can reduce stress, sleep well, and get daily support from their family.

chosen.khen3Text: a safe and practical choice that lets the student stay in a supportive environment, build confidence, and get ready for a stable career.

rejected.reason: choosing a university just because the tuition fee is cheap is not wise, because the student might have to study a major they dislike, and classes with low tuition are often too crowded for students to ask teachers questions.

focusing only on a high ranking often leads to top-ranked universities with high tuition fees or expensive apartment rent far from home, which can force parents to borrow money and create constant financial worry for the whole family.

title: Part 3 - Topic 2: The Importance of Music Education
content:
Topic: The importance of music education for students
Suggestions:
- Fostering creativity and emotional expression
- Reducing academic stress and improving mental well-being
- Enhancing memory, focus, and discipline
- [Your own ideas]

Follow-up questions:
1. Should music be a compulsory subject in primary and secondary schools?
2. What challenges do schools face when offering quality music education?
3. How can parents encourage their children to appreciate music?

hint.coreTopic: the importance of music education for students

followUps.answer: Yes, I think schools should keep music as a compulsory subject in primary and secondary schools to support students' healthy development.
followUps.example: For instance, one 45-minute music lesson per week helps secondary students stay relaxed and learn teamwork when singing in a school choir.
followUps.q: Should music be a compulsory subject in primary and secondary schools?
followUps.reason: Music gives students needed downtime from heavy academic pressure and allows every child to explore their talents regardless of family income.

followUps.answer: There are some challenges schools face, such as a lack of musical instruments, limited budgets, and not enough trained music teachers.
followUps.example: For example, many rural schools only have one old keyboard for a class of 40 students to share.
followUps.q: What challenges do schools face when offering quality music education?
followUps.reason: Many schools focus mainly on math and languages, so they do not invest enough money into upgrading music rooms and modern teaching tools.

followUps.answer: I think parents should guide and support their children gently by letting them listen to good music and choose an instrument they truly like.
followUps.example: For example, parents can play relaxing music at home during dinner or let their child try a 30-minute weekend guitar class.
followUps.q: How can parents encourage their children to appreciate music?
followUps.reason: Forcing children too hard creates stress and family conflicts, while patient support helps children enjoy music naturally.

mindmapPoints.expand: because playing instruments or singing allows their brain to exercise creatively and helps them share feelings naturally.
mindmapPoints.impact: Therefore, it is good for students' creative thinking.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Learning music helps students develop creativity and express their emotions.

mindmapPoints.cue: Reducing academic stress and improving mental well-being
mindmapPoints.expand: For example, having a music class after hard math or science lessons lets children unwind, relax, and elevate their mood.
mindmapPoints.impact: Clearly, it is beneficial to students' mental health.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Music education helps students relieve study stress and feel happier.

mindmapPoints.expand: This is because learning to play a song requires regular daily practice, which trains patience and boosts school efficiency.
mindmapPoints.impact: So, it has positive effects on their overall study results.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Practicing music helps learners improve their memory, focus, and self-discipline.
